text: The per-stat CAP formulas diverge between builds in four of six rows, and one of them feeds the reach model directly. Positionally aligned, same six handlers in the same order: MAXHP web '10 + (lvl+10)*10' vs android '10 + (lvl+10)*5'; MAXCHI identical in both; MAXAP web '30 + (lvl+10)*5' vs android '20 + (lvl+10)'; ATK/DEF/SPD web '1 + (lvl+10)*3' vs android 'lvl + 10'. This makes the web level-8 Dan-0 reach ceiling 120 + floor(90*55/75) = 186, not the ~130 an android-capped reading gives.

text: The web v0.717 build is not data-free. It embeds 27 XML/binary blobs: nineteen <animdata> tables (100-118), one <survivalmodedata> (119), one room-object definition file (93), five name tables (94-98) and one GIF89a (92). What it does NOT embed is the four gameplay tables — itemdata, skilldata, npcdata, questdata — which it URL-loads. Any restatement of 'the web build ships no data XML at all' must be narrowed to those four or it contradicts the Stage-0 S0-1 inventory.

Measured by raw occurrence of `<skill><id>NNNN</id><lvl>` over the whole file: 1500 (Reversed-stance mastery) 5 rows at lines 3662, 3683, 3898, 4290, 4349, all <lvl>3</lvl>; 1501 (Dual-stance mastery) 2 rows at 3934, 3956, both <lvl>3</lvl>; 1064 4 rows (3898, 3934, 3956, 4290); 1065 4 rows (same four); 1066 1 row (3879); 1067 1 row (3879); 1068 (SkillManager.SKILL_UNDYING) 2 rows — 3934 at <lvl>1</lvl> and 4349 at <lvl>2</lvl>. text: The COINS/GOLD dual-currency HUD strip is real and I have opened it — but it is NOT in frame_0027, which NF-2/coins-and-gold cites. frame_0027 is a 'YOU RECEIVED' loot dialog on a full-screen red freeze (coin icon + 15, 'XP 510', three PANTS slots, OK button) with no HUD strip at all. The strip appears in the same directory at frame_0029, frame_0030, frame_0040, frame_0041 and frame_0042. Visible in the top band, left to right: a silver coin icon with '480' over the label 'COINS'; a red '+' button; a gold coin icon with '2' over the label 'GOLD'; a red 'GET GOLD' button; and at the right a level badge '7' beside a yellow bar reading '14901 / 16350' over 'EXPERIENCE POINTS'. 16350 is expArray[7], consistent with a level-7 player. The code mapping the claim pairs with it is sound: STAT_GOLD = id 11 renders as COINS and STAT_HGOLD = id 12 renders as GOLD, and character creation sets 11 -> 100 and 12 -> 3. THE FRAME WINS: bank frame_0029, not frame_0027.

lane_impact: L5 combat-core: promotes the Heavy def x0.8 term from android-plus-skill-description to a two-site web v0.717 fact, and establishes that the v0.717 character sheet is a trustworthy cross-check on the sim (the v0.682 one demonstrably is not).
text: Heavy-stance Defence x0.8 has a THIRD confirmation nobody has banked, and it is entirely web-side — no android string and no wiki. The web v0.717 character sheet sets its defence modifier per stance at §1t5957s0§.as:2728 (light = 1), :2737 (balanced = 1) and :2746 (heavy = 0.8), and consumes it at :2947 as `int(_loc3_ * _loc47_)` beside the stance name — the positional twin of android InventoryUI.as:2166 `"physical def: " + int(defense * defModifier) + " (" + stanceName + ")"`. So in v0.717 the character sheet and the simulation AGREE on defence (§1t99s0§.as:3288 `return defense * 0.8;`), unlike the android build where they contradict each other on crit. That agreement is itself worth banking: it means the v0.717 char-sheet path is a usable cross-check, whereas the v0.682 one is not.

text: UNCLAIMED AND LANE-RELEVANT: the web v0.717 character sheet carries a per-stance SLASH-DISTANCE ladder that no claim in this packet touches, and it is the mirror image of the damage ladder. In the same three stance branches that set damage and crit, §1t5957s0§.as sets a fourth modifier: :2729 light = 1.4 flat; :2738 balanced = 1 + 0.2*balancedMastery*0.1; :2747 heavy = 0.5 + 0.4*heavyMastery*0.1. It is not yet shown that the v0.717 sim uses the same coefficients — that needs the InputManager.setMaxDistance call site in the web bundle. What it does do is give the reach question its first ratio-shaped web-build evidence, and it is not a static text field, so SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md:33-36's placeholder ruling does not apply to it.

text: All five XOR-obfuscated Android resource blobs decrypt and inflate, and 115_Mobile_SHS3Resource.bin IS the per-item art manifest. The cipher is in the corpus: ResourceManager.as:200-217 decryptByteArray touches only bytes 3..255 (with an i%11==0 swap to i+256) and the key is the SECOND CHARACTER OF THE RESOURCE FILENAME - Mobile.as:352 / ResourceManager.as:186 pass resourceFileNameArray[n].charCodeAt(1), and ResourceManager.as:41 names the five files. Keys are therefore h=104 (shs3resource), u=117 (musicresource), o=111 (soundresource), m=109 (imageresource), g=103 (bgresource). Running that over all five: 115 -> 1,040,849 B, 113 -> 1,402,677 B, 122 -> 29,623 B, 124 -> 1,908,229 B, 120 -> 4,412,340 B, every one a CWS v17 that zlib-inflates cleanly. Parsing SymbolClass/ExportAssets out of the inflated 115 yields 1,912 exported symbols whose prefixes are exactly the getMCSComponent partTypes: torso/stomach/uparm/lowarm/pelvic 151 each, item 112, weapon 109, hat 96, calf/crotch/thigh 85 each, skill 79, hair 73, prop 60, mask 59, foot/foottop 44 each, head 38, hand/neck 33 each, backleg/frontleg 12 each, tail 9, acc 8, achievement 5, plus *_wolf_ and *_horse_ creature sets. Sample names: item0, item1, item009, item010, item2100..., acc3000..acc3008, weapon13000..weapon13056. NOTE the C1 brief gives key 'm'=109 as the example; that is the IMAGE resource key specifically, not a single key for all five.

lane_impact: L6 (art/animation) - the creature-rig contract is not 'human 23 + 4 extras'. A wolf gets a fresh 26-slot block stacked on top of the inherited 23, and the PART_* indices 23-26 address the new block. Anyone porting the quadruped rig from the packet's partList claims will build the wrong container count and the wrong z-order for creatures.
quote: MCSWolf.as:11 'super();' / :13 'partListLength = 25;' / :14 'for(var i:int = 0; i <= partListLength; i++)' / :17 'partList.push(mc);'  ||  MCSCharacter.as:141 'for(var i:int = 0; i <= this.partListLength; i++)' with :120 'internal var partListLength:int = 22;'  ||  MCSCharacter.as:246 'for(var i:* = int(this.partListLength - 1); i >= 0; i--)'
text: MCSWolf's partList ends up 49 entries long, not 26. Its constructor calls super() FIRST (MCSWolf.as:11), which runs MCSCharacter's own loop and pushes 23 clips (indices 0..22); only then does it set partListLength = 25 (:13) and push 26 MORE (:14-18). Indices 23-26, which MCSWolf then binds as leg segments at :184/:188/:193/:197, therefore land in the second batch. Every claim in this packet that says 'MCSWolf raises partListLength to 25' is right about the field and silent about the list. A second consequence: MCSCharacter.as:246 'for(var i:* = int(this.partListLength - 1); i >= 0; i--)' walks only indices 24..0 on a wolf, so it never touches the upper half of that 49-entry list.
